prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1229; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver. Reports a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Vehicle is drivable but front bumper, hood and radiator support appear damaged. Claimant states she was stopped and believes the other vehicle crossed the center line. Assigned to adjuster for initial contact and photo request.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. She reports her wrist struck the steering wheel during airbag deployment and she was later seen at an urgent care facility, where an X-ray indicated a fracture. She has no attorney and says she prefers to handle the claim directly. Explained the claim process, requested the urgent care records and the imaging report, and asked for a signed medical authorization.

Entry 3: Received photos of both vehicles and the police report from the reporting agency. Report notes no citations issued and lists the other driver as at fault for crossing into the opposing lane. Damage to the claimant's vehicle is consistent with the description given. Other driver's carrier has been notified and an accident liability file opened.

Entry 4: Claimant returned the signed medical authorization and forwarded the discharge paperwork. Advised that the bodily injury portion will be evaluated once treatment is complete and records from the orthopedic follow-up are received. Reminded claimant she may request a rental vehicle under her coverage and she indicated she would like one arranged while her car is in the shop.

Entry 5: Obtained repair estimate from a preferred shop and total damage is under the vehicle's actual cash value, so repair is recommended. Other carrier has accepted liability for property damage in principle. Bodily injury claim remains open pending orthopedic records. Diary set to follow up with claimant in two weeks for treatment status and to confirm rental is in place.
